summary.intent: Resolve 6 CodeRabbit review threads on PR #485 by implementing fixes, posting replies, and marking threads resolved, then address a follow-up outside-diff comment about test assertion ordering.
summary.outcome: All 6 threads fixed, replied to, and resolved with CI fully green (Lint, Typecheck, Test, Build, SDK E2E, Verify API Spec & Client). A 7th fix (test ordering assertion for callOrder[2]) was applied from an outside-diff comment and committed.

repo: In apps/web, vitest's `include` pattern is `*.test.ts` — files named `*.spec.ts` are silently excluded and never run. The delete.service spec was renamed from .spec.ts to .test.ts to fix this.
Automated GSD/Entire commits bypass the husky pre-commit hook (which would auto-fix prettier errors), so CI's `eslint .` is the only backstop for lint issues introduced by those commits.

Running `openapi:generate` alone produces ~700 lines of array-formatting noise because it skips the `lint:fix` step that the full `api:generate` pipeline runs — the committed spec is always correct per CI's Verify API Spec & Client check.
Rust CI jobs are always skipped (3 jobs) — this is expected behavior, not a failure.
zsh uses 1-based arrays, which caused an off-by-one error when iterating review thread IDs via shell array indexing, resulting in two missed API posts.

code.finding: guardedUnpin now accepts a `suppressCrossUserAudit` option; internal rollback paths pass this to avoid emitting false cross-user security metrics while public /unpin still audits.
Scheduler init failure handling: fail fast (error+rethrow) in production, warn+continue in other envs to avoid throwing in test/E2E contexts.
Kubo pin/ls fetch is bounded with AbortSignal.timeout(30_000) to prevent hanging workers.
Advisory lock merged into a single pg_advisory_xact_lock(abs(hashtext($1))::bigint) call as the first statement; ordering test updated.
fetchQuota returns a success boolean (no-throw contract) rather than rejecting, to avoid unhandled-rejection blast radius across ~5 fire-and-forget callers; deleteFile warns on false return.
Script now tracks failedBatches and calls exit(1) on any failure instead of always exiting 0.

Test named 'then fetchQuota in order' was not asserting callOrder[2] === 'fetchQuota'; added expect(callOrder[2]).toBe('fetchQuota') and changed mockFetchQuota assertion to toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) for clarity.

workflow: When posting multiple GitHub API replies via shell loops, avoid array indexing across network calls — post each reply explicitly with hardcoded IDs to avoid zsh 1-based array off-by-one errors and i/o timeout skips.
Writing reply bodies to temp files before posting avoids shell-escaping issues with backticks and special characters in GitHub REST API calls.
CodeRabbit outside-diff comments are not resolvable threads — they require code fixes only, with no GraphQL thread resolution needed.
Batching GraphQL thread resolutions into a single mutation is more reliable than sequential resolution calls.

friction: zsh 1-based array indexing caused two review thread replies to be missed (thread [0] and [5]), requiring a second explicit posting pass.
Thread [0] also hit a network i/o timeout during the initial batch post, compounding the miss.
Running openapi:generate standalone produced 700 lines of spurious diff noise, causing a spec-drift false alarm that required investigation to rule out.
open_items: CodeRabbit is re-reviewing commit 407578bf1 — its findings are non-blocking but may generate additional threads to address.
The ~5 fire-and-forget callers of fetchQuota were not migrated to handle the new boolean return — they silently ignore quota fetch failures, which is acceptable for now but could mask issues.

The deviated approach on pending-unpin.module.ts (warn+continue in non-production instead of CodeRabbit's dev-only check) may warrant revisiting if test/E2E environments need stricter scheduler init guarantees.
